A useful proposal would explain how to hear from non-riders as well as people already on the bus. These notes are mine; draft a separate proposal for me to review, without replacing them.

blocks.heading: Recommendation
blocks.content: Given these limits, I propose extending the pilot for one term rather than ending or permanently expanding it. A single-term commitment avoids locking in long-term funding before I understand who actually uses the service and why. The 160 and 240 weekly boardings suggest interest, but without non-rider input, I cannot determine whether demand is broad or niche [@lyra:1]. Keeping the pilot running buys time to gather the missing data while maintaining the status quo. This conditional approach allows me to test access barriers directly, ensuring that any future expansion rests on verified demand rather than assumption. The extension itself costs little compared to the expense of guessing wrong later.

blocks.content: During the extension, I will implement two low-cost data collection methods to address the current gaps. First, I will survey non-riders to identify barriers to entry and gauge potential interest, since the initial pilot only captured responses from current users [@lyra:2]. The goal is to verify if the 160 to 240 weekly boardings reflect a growing pattern or a transient spike before committing to further expansion.

# My shuttle memo notes

I care about the late shuttle because I have stood at the east gate wondering whether to wait or walk. I want the memo to admit that this is my starting point. It is not a campus-wide survey. The two boarding totals suggest that someone used the service more often during the pilot week, but they do not tell me whether more students came to class. I should not make a number answer a question it was never asked.

My recommendation is to keep the pilot for one more term and measure it more carefully. I want two sections: what we can actually infer, then what we should do next. Please keep the uncertainty visible. Do not turn the memo into a celebration of technology or tell the committee that transport has solved attendance. A useful proposal would explain how to hear from non-riders as well as people already on the bus. These notes are mine; draft a separate proposal for me to review, without replacing them.

# My shuttle memo notes

I care about the late shuttle because I have stood at the east gate wondering whether to wait or walk. I want the memo to admit that this is my starting point. It is not a campus-wide survey. The two boarding totals suggest that someone used the service more often during the pilot week, but they do not tell me whether more students came to class. I should not make a number answer a question it was never asked.

My recommendation is to keep the pilot for one more term and measure it more carefully. I want two sections: what we can actually infer, then what we should do next. Please keep the uncertainty visible. Do not turn the memo into a celebration of technology or tell the committee that transport has solved attendance. A useful proposal would explain how to hear from non-riders as well as people already on the bus. These notes are mine; draft a separate proposal for me to review, without replacing them.

live_draft_blocks.heading: Recommendation
live_draft_blocks.content: Because the current data remain provisional, I propose extending the pilot for one term rather than ending or permanently expanding it. This conditional step directly addresses the representativeness gap by allowing time to collect the missing non-rider data without committing to indefinite operation. A single-term commitment avoids locking in long-term resources before I understand who actually uses the service and why. While the 160 and 240 weekly boardings suggest interest, the absence of non-rider input prevents me from determining whether demand is broad or niche [@lyra:1]. Keeping the pilot running buys the necessary time to gather this evidence while maintaining the status quo. This approach allows me to test access barriers directly, ensuring that any future expansion rests on verified demand rather than assumption.

live_draft_blocks.content: During the extension, I will implement two low-cost data collection methods to address the current gaps. First, I will survey non-riders to identify barriers to entry and gauge potential interest, since the initial pilot only captured responses from current users [@lyra:2]. Second, I will log basic attendance figures alongside boarding counts to correlate service usage with overall student presence, a metric absent from the original records [@lyra:1]. These steps will clarify whether demand is limited to a small group or broad enough to support long-term service. The goal is to verify if the 160 to 240 weekly boardings reflect a growing pattern or a transient spike before committing to further expansion.
